reason: The two are identical except for the peach circle at bottom left. Shared flaws: the can is shrunk to a small mark, leaving a large dead gap between it and the headline. The sage circle now sits behind the SOLSTICE wordmark and touches the can's sun icon. The body copy and the CTA label are very small (about 11px) for a story format, and the wide empty bands make the column feel stretched rather than redesigned. In A the peach circle stays clear of the Find a Store button. In B it is larger and runs under the button's left end, adding a collision that the original avoided.

Both share the same core flaws: the legal line is enlarged and jammed directly under the headline, above the CTA, so the fine print competes with the message and splits headline from button. The badge and logo are also split to opposite top corners with no shared axis. A's headline runs almost edge to edge with an awkward 'day of / the year' break. B wraps the headline better ('day / of the year') with comfortable margins, but it moves the large translucent planet directly behind the can, which muddies the product silhouette.

Both are shrunk 320x50 strips with the same flaws: the legal fine print is promoted to a prominent left-hand block as large as secondary copy and crowds the tiny logo/can stack, and the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is shrunk to an illegible sliver under the headline. A's headline is smaller and breaks awkwardly ('...day of / the year...'), leaving loose dead space around it. B's headline is larger and dominant, but it presses up against the CTA and its ribbon is even more cramped, so B is only marginally better on hierarchy.

Both put the legal fine print first on the far left, about as large as the subhead, so it competes with the message and the logo is barely visible. In A, the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon collides with the phone mockup, and the two-line headline plus the subhead are jammed into the full height of the banner. In B, the headline sits cleanly on one line above the subhead, but the ribbon is shrunk and pushed against the bottom edge under the subhead, where it reads as an afterthought. B is slightly cleaner overall.

A breaks the product art: the can floats away from its circle, and the body copy sits on top of the circle, jammed against the left edge, which is a clear text-on-graphic collision. The GLACIER wordmark also drops below the headline, and the badges are oversized, so they compete with the CTA. B keeps the can inside its circle and the headline and CTA group reads cleanly. But B has a large dead area on the left, and the body copy is split off to the far right edge, after the product, so the reading order is wrong. The badges in B are too large, and 'BACK BYDEMAND' is missing a space.

A: the body copy is shrunk to an unreadable block crammed against the bottom-right edge. GROVE sits below the headline, which inverts the brand order. The CTA, badges and tilted FREE DELIVERY tag are all squeezed into one cluttered row, and the product circle is small and floats in the top-left. B: the body copy is legible on a single line and the product circle is larger, but GROVE still sits under the headline. Its stack is tight and runs right up to the bottom edge, and the CTA has been reduced to a tiny pill no bigger than the badges, so the hierarchy is weak.

A rebuilds the layout badly. The headline is blown up into two huge lines that crowd the right column, and the CTA is bloated. The tagline is pulled away from the headline and stranded top-right above the button. The flavour chips are reversed and jammed under the CTA, nearly touching the headline's 'here', and the SOLSTICE wordmark is shrunk. B keeps the original hierarchy, grid and chip order nearly intact. Its only issues are minor: the decorative circles are enlarged, so the yellow one sits behind the headline and chips and the pink one frames the CTA more heavily than in the original, and the chip labels are still tiny.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark has dropped below the headline, so the reading order is wrong. The flavour pills are microscopic with unreadable text and run in reversed order. The subcopy and CTA sit off-axis over the peach circle. Still, A keeps the original's two-circle composition and the pills are consistent with each other. B has the same wrong brand placement and the same off-axis CTA. On top of that, it moves the peach circle onto the yellow one, which leaves the bottom-right empty. Its pills are inconsistent: CUCUMBER MINT is smaller, raised and nearly illegible, and the row starts left of the text column, so it looks more broken.

A moves the peach circle on top of the yellow circles in the top-left, making a muddy orange blob. Its pills are uneven: Cucumber Mint is smaller and sits higher than the others, the row starts left of the text column, and the pill order is reversed. B keeps the original circles and lays out a clean, evenly spaced pill row on the text's left edge. Both share the same flaws: the SOLSTICE wordmark drops below the headline, which breaks the reading order. The CTA floats off the text axis, and the pill labels are nearly illegible. B's subcopy also runs almost to the right edge of the canvas.

A: the 'NEW' badge and the 'Try It' button both sit on top of the shrunken product circle, so three elements collide in one cramped middle cluster. The subcopy is pushed to the far right as a narrow three-line ragged block, which breaks the reading order (headline, then badge/product/CTA, then copy), and the headline wraps awkwardly onto two lines. B: it keeps the original left-to-right structure, clear hierarchy and brand colours, but it is essentially a straight shrink. The subcopy and the 'NEW' pill text are around 5px and barely legible, the product circle is cropped at the top and left edges, and there is dead space between the copy and the badge.

A keeps the product art intact: the can sits on its cream circle. But the headline is small and jammed top-left, the subtitle is tiny, the NEW and Try It buttons are undersized, and big empty orange gaps break up the layout. B has the same weak text and buttons, and it also breaks the product: the cream circle has moved to a cropped bottom-left corner, so the orange can disappears into the orange background and only the dark label and two green dots stay visible.

A: the legal text opens the banner on the far left in four wrapped lines, almost as prominent as the message, and it crowds the tiny can and logo; the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is shrunk to an illegible sliver jammed under 'longer', and the headline is small next to the CTA. B has the same backwards reading order (legal copy and a cramped can on the left) and the ribbon is still unreadably small, but its headline is larger and sets a clearer hierarchy, and the ribbon has a little more space below the headline. That makes B marginally the less broken of two poor results.

A keeps the original structure almost exactly: the hierarchy is clean, the left column and chips are aligned, and the CTA stands clear. Its only issue is that the peach circle now sits as a full disc behind the CTA, which makes the right side feel a little heavy. B is oversized and cramped. The two-line headline is huge and almost touches the flavour chips. The chips are in reverse order and their tiny text is jammed into the lower-right corner. The subcopy is moved above the button and pushed against the top edge, and the oversized CTA competes with the headline.

Both demote the SOLSTICE wordmark to below the headline, reverse the order of the flavour pills, centre the CTA under a left-aligned text column and leave a dead area at the bottom left. A also stacks the peach circle awkwardly inside the yellow one and drops the bottom-right accent circle. Its pills are mismatched in size and misaligned: Cucumber Mint is smaller and sits higher, and the row starts left of the text column. B keeps the original's two-circle composition and lines the pills up with the text column, though the pill labels are too small to read and the peach circle crowds behind the CTA and subcopy.

Both candidates put the SOLSTICE wordmark below the headline, which breaks the reading order. Both also have pill text that is too small to read, and both float the CTA off the text column's left edge. A keeps the three pills equal in size and aligned to the column, with the peach circle sitting behind the CTA much as in the original. B moves the peach circle onto the yellow one, which muddies the top-left decoration. Its pills are ragged: Honey Rosemary starts left of the column, and Cucumber Mint is smaller and sits higher, with even tinier text. B's pills are also jammed against the CTA.

Both share the same flawed stack: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline instead of above it, there is a dead gap between the body copy and the small can, and the headline breaks awkwardly as 'Garden-fresh / fizz'. A piles both decorative circles into one overlapping blob in the bottom-left, which loses the original's opposite-corner balance and leaves the top empty. B keeps the green circle top-right and the peach circle bottom-left as in the original, though the green circle runs behind the 'fresh' of the headline, a minor collision with a flat shape.

A and B are almost the same: a shrunk bottle with a large dead gap above the headline, tiny low-contrast body copy, a small CTA, and the 'SOLSTICE' wordmark sitting on the edge of the green circle. In A, the larger peach circle runs under the left end of the 'Find a Store' button, an unwanted collision. In B the circle is smaller and stays clear of the button, so B is the less bad resize.

A keeps the can inside its circle backdrop, so the product imagery survives. But the GLACIER wordmark sits below the headline, the body copy is shrunk to illegible micro-text and jammed beside the badges, the CTA row is pressed against the bottom edge, and a large dead area is left on the left. B pulls the circle away from the can, leaving a meaningless empty disc on the left and a can floating with no backdrop. It also has GLACIER below the headline and a small CTA that gets no more weight than the badges, though its body copy is readable and its text block is tidier.

Both use the same broken 320x50 layout. The legal disclaimer is blown up to the size of the body copy and fills the right third. The SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline instead of above it. The three flavour pills don't match in size, and the subline is too small to read. In A, the Blood Orange pill is jammed against the top edge, clipped and crowding the CTA, and the subline is crushed beneath the button. B is marginally less bad: its Blood Orange pill is tiny but sits cleanly under the CTA, though its subline is unreadable and jammed into the top-left corner.

A keeps the original's left-column stack (eyebrow, headline, body, pill CTA) with the bottle over the peach circle. Its alignment and hierarchy are clean. The only nitpicks are the tight gap between the 'off' headline and the circle edge and slightly cramped bottom spacing. B breaks the reading order. The body copy sits above the headline, squeezed into a narrow 5-line column ('Every / mixed / case of…') jammed against the bottle. The headline is split into '20% / off' and pushed to the bottom-left, 'WEEKEND ONLY' wraps awkwardly, the brand circle is cropped into a small fragment, and the oversized CTA crowds the bottle and the right edge.

The two candidates are effectively identical, so I scored this pair a tie with the same score. In both, the RSVP Free CTA has shrunk to the size of the Free Entry/All Ages/Tastings pills, so the call to action is lost among the badges. The time and venue line is split off from 'Saturday 21 June' and pushed to the far right, past the product can. The SOLSTICE logo is tiny and isolated at the far right. 'Reserve a spot' sits under the subtitle in a crowded left column, which jumbles the reading order. There is also a stray red fragment after the Tastings pill, left over from the missing partner asset.

A shrinks the bottle, the hero product, to a tiny thumbnail tucked in the top-right circle where it can't be read, so the product is lost. Its body copy sits on the yellow circle at very small size, jammed into the bottom-left corner, and the oversized headline dominates the whole canvas. B keeps the bottle large on the left, layered over the green circle, so it reads left to right as a banner should. Its flaws: SOLSTICE sits under the headline in heavy spaced caps and competes with it, the body copy is tiny, and the yellow circle leaves the bottom-right corner empty.

A keeps a coherent centred stack and readable hierarchy, but the headline leaves 'last' orphaned on its own line, the legal line is moved above an oversized CTA that competes with the headline, and the sale banner is pushed against the top-left edge. B leaves a large dead area beside the bottle, which sits awkwardly left of centre. Its bottom row crams the subcopy into a narrow wrapped column and the legal text into a tiny 7-line sliver either side of the CTA, all pressed toward the bottom edge, which breaks the reading order and makes the fine print hard to read.

A keeps the can inside its circle and puts headline, brand and buttons in a sensible left-to-right group. Reading order starts with that body copy, and the 'SUMMER ONLY' badge text is tiny.

Both candidates have the same broken structure. The CTA comes first on the left, ahead of the brand and headline. The SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline instead of above it. The flavour pills are in reverse order. The subcopy is squeezed into a cramped two-line block beside the pills. The legal text floats to the right at about the same weight as the subcopy, leaving a large dead gap in the middle. B is slightly worse: its CTA is jammed against the left canvas edge, and the decorative circle is pushed to the far right, so the left half reads as cramped. A keeps a margin and keeps the circles behind the button.

Both share the same broken layout. The steps are out of order (01 at top, above the eyebrow, then 03, then 02), and the step copy is shrunk to illegible micro-text scattered across the canvas. The legal line is set larger than the steps, and the logo is demoted to a footer beside it. A keeps the beige circle in the top-right corner as in the original. B moves the circle behind 'cup' and the step-03 line, which clutters the headline area and is slightly worse.

A reads cleanly left to right with the badge, box, headline and CTA inside the framed lime panel, but the 48H badge is jammed against the left edge, the subcopy is squeezed into a tiny three-line block, and the box and badge are cramped together. A: the 'Find It Near You' CTA has shrunk to a small pill jammed into the top-left corner next to the badges. That buries the CTA, and 'SUMMER ONLY' wraps onto a second line out of alignment. Both are nearly identical and broken in the same ways. Both have the same broken layout: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' sits below the event details, the URL line comes before the time/venue, the text stack is jammed together with uneven left/centre alignment, and the RSVP CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill mixed in with the badges at the bottom, so the call to action is buried. The only difference is the decorative circle: A keeps the original's large circle behind the headline, while B shrinks it to an odd little blob in the corner, so A stays slightly closer to the original.

Both have the same flaws. The SOLSTICE brand sits below the headline, so the reading order is wrong. The pills are reversed and jammed together, and the subhead is shrunk to illegible fine print squeezed beside them. The left third holds nothing but decorative circles while the centre is overcrowded. A's oversized CTA nearly touches the top and bottom canvas edges and its pills collide; B's slightly smaller CTA has a little more margin, which makes it marginally less cramped.
